target_style: Environmental Health revision; double-column quantitative figures

export_contract.height_mm: figure-specific; see exported PDF page sizes

shared_target_definition: For count-scale target panels, A denotes the expected count contrast: factual path minus the 1°C cooler counterfactual path. Do not call this disease burden or incidence.

figure_1_fixed_design.source_figure: fixed-design interval coverage and error scale
figure_1_fixed_design.core_conclusion: Across the three predeclared fixed-design scenarios and three fixed seeds, interval coverage and reported error scale vary by covariance method; all methods remain visible, including the under-covering and ineffective comparisons.

panel_map.A-C: Planned-denominator coverage across model-compatible, response-misspecification and omitted-confounding scenarios; one panel per scenario, three seeds and five covariance methods.
panel_map.D-F: Mean method-specific SE and empirical sample SD of estimation error for the same scenario/seed/method cells.

figure_1_fixed_design.n_definition: Each point uses 1,000 planned test repetitions for one design seed and scenario. Fit failures and method-specific invalid intervals count as uncovered. Three fixed seeds and all 45 method × scenario × seed rows are shown.
figure_1_fixed_design.uncertainty_definition: Coverage whiskers are ±1 binomial MCSE using the planned denominator. Open circles show arithmetic mean positive finite method SE among coefficient-fit successes with valid method variance; exact per-point n is n_mean_standard_error. Filled squares show sample SD (ddof=1) of A_hat − A_true among coefficient-fit successes; exact per-point n is n_empirical_error_sd.
figure_1_fixed_design.source_data: Frozen formal fixed-design summary and per-replicate panel rows; plotted source table and row hashes are in QA.
reviewer_risks: Do not use pilot results.
Keep failures and invalid intervals in the planned coverage denominator.
Mean-SE and empirical-SD denominators differ and are labeled separately.

figure_2_heatday_fixed_design.source_figure: heat-day fixed-design interval coverage and error scale
figure_2_heatday_fixed_design.core_conclusion: Across model-compatible and source-quadratic designs, the component-specific two-way CR1 interval has lower coverage than the legacy and corrected-common intervals; coverage varies by method in the common-bias design, whose scenario-specific truth changes.

panel_map.A-C: Planned-denominator coverage for model-compatible, source-quadratic and quadratic plus shared temporal term scenarios; three fixed seeds and five covariance methods per scenario.
panel_map.D-F: Mean method-specific SE and empirical sample SD of A_hat − A_true for those same scenario/seed/method cells.

figure_2_heatday_fixed_design.n_definition: Each point uses 1,000 planned test-stage repetitions for one scenario and seed. Three fixed seeds are shown in each of three scenarios. Training and calibration stages are excluded from test summaries.
figure_2_heatday_fixed_design.uncertainty_definition: Coverage whiskers are ±1 binomial MCSE using the planned denominator. Mean SE uses valid positive finite method-specific SEs; exact per-point denominator is n_mean_standard_error. Empirical error SD is sample SD (ddof=1) among coefficient-fit successes; exact per-point denominator is n_empirical_error_sd.
figure_2_heatday_fixed_design.target_semantics: A_true is the expected count contrast sum(mu − mu_cf) for each fixed design. Cholecystectomy labels refer to hospital admission/discharge records; death labels refer to all-cause registered deaths where applicable.
reviewer_risks: The common-bias design has its own scenario-specific A_true; do not treat it as a same-truth comparison.
Keep fit failures and invalid intervals in coverage denominator.
Do not call the target disease burden or incidence.
figure_2_heatday_fixed_design.scenario_definition: The common-bias heat-day DGP adds the shared temporal term 0.12 z; the source scenario and its frozen results are preserved.

figure_3_observed_and_formal.source_figure: observed specification sensitivity and formal interval coverage
figure_3_observed_and_formal.core_conclusion: Observed daily estimates and known-truth repeated-sampling coverage answer different questions; each case retains the full nine-specification observed grid and all three formal scenarios across Poisson, HAC14, HAC28 and Quasi-Poisson.

panel_map.A,C: Observed expected-count contrasts and nominal 90% intervals over the nine predeclared specifications for the state and city-matched cases.
panel_map.B,D: Formal planned-denominator coverage in the compatible, omitted seasonal interaction and correlated-overdispersed AR(1) scenarios for both cases.

figure_3_observed_and_formal.n_definition: Observed panels use 1,805 daily outcomes per specification. Formal coverage uses 1,000 planned replications per case and scenario; failed fits count as uncovered.
figure_3_observed_and_formal.uncertainty_definition: Observed intervals are nominal 90% source intervals. Formal whiskers are ±1 binomial MCSE.
figure_3_observed_and_formal.target_semantics: Observed estimates are expected count contrasts: factual path minus 1°C cooler path.
reviewer_risks: Do not infer causal identification from model-based observed-data intervals.
Keep observed estimates separate from known-truth empirical coverage.
The omitted seasonal interaction scenario is distinct from the shared 0.12 z heat-day term.

figure_4_mechanism_diagnostic.core_conclusion: The known-truth diagnostic separates deterministic projection bias, finite-sample mean error and error-scale mismatch under compatible, omitted seasonal interaction and correlated AR(1) scenarios; oracle benchmarks are explanatory controls.

panel_map.A,D: Deterministic projection bias and empirical mean error with ±1 MCSE, for state and city cases.
panel_map.B,E: Mean reported SE divided by empirical error SD for Poisson, Quasi-Poisson, HAC14, HAC28 and the linearized known-process oracle.
panel_map.C,F: Coverage of oracle-scale and oracle-scale plus known-bias centering benchmarks.

figure_4_mechanism_diagnostic.n_definition: Each case and scenario uses 1,000 planned and converged formal replications.
figure_4_mechanism_diagnostic.scenario_definition: The omitted seasonal interaction is the daily-data mechanism scenario; do not label it as the shared 0.12 z heat-day term.
reviewer_risks: Ancillary diagnostic, not a new applied method comparison.
Oracle scale and known-bias centering are controls, not deployable procedures.
Overlap of Monte Carlo bars with 0.90 is not evidence that coverage equals nominal.

figure_S1_lagweight_delta.source_figure: monthly sensitivity radius across lag allocations and delta
figure_S1_lagweight_delta.core_conclusion: The complete 4-panel × 5-allocation × 4-delta finite-grid display compares each deterministic sensitivity radius with its stored base 90% interval half-width.

axis_definitions.x: Predeclared delta on the log-risk perturbation scale: 0.01, 0.025, 0.05 and 0.10.
axis_definitions.fill: Sensitivity radius divided by stored base 90% interval half-width; dimensionless.

figure_S1_lagweight_delta.n_definition: All 80 rows are shown: four panels × five lag allocations × four delta values.
figure_S1_lagweight_delta.uncertainty_definition: The tile values are deterministic finite-grid sensitivity ratios, not sampling uncertainty or empirical coverage.
figure_S1_lagweight_delta.source_data: Source table, plotted values and parsed-row SHA-256 hashes are recorded in qa/figure_sources_sensitivity_grid.csv and .json.
reviewer_risks: Retain all 80 panel × lag-allocation × delta combinations.
Describe the class as finite observed-grid and fixed allocation; do not imply a continuous-temperature certificate.
Do not call the ratios sampling coverage, disease burden, or incidence.

figure_S2_deterministic_displacement.source_figure: within-class bound checks and out-of-class zero-sum lag-transfer displacement
figure_S2_deterministic_displacement.core_conclusion: All 16 fixed-allocation within-class checks remain below their stored deterministic class envelope; the 24 out-of-class zero-sum lag-transfer checks are shown only for scale comparison.

panel_map.A: Maximum exact expected-count contrast shift divided by the stored uniform bound, across four outcomes and four delta values at fixed 0.50 / 0.50 lag allocation.
panel_map.B: Absolute exact expected-count contrast shift relative to the delta=0.05 fixed-allocation envelope, plotted against maximum row log-predictor shift for 24 out-of-class zero-sum lag transfers.

figure_S2_deterministic_displacement.n_definition: Panel a contains 16 panel × delta checks, each summarizing 272 deterministic candidates (four polygon vertices, 12 edge-convex combinations and 256 predeclared radial directions). Panel b contains 24 deterministic out-of-class checks.
figure_S2_deterministic_displacement.uncertainty_definition: Both panels display deterministic calculations with no sampling uncertainty, Monte Carlo error, or empirical coverage estimate.
figure_S2_deterministic_displacement.target_semantics: Displacement is on the expected count contrast scale: factual path minus the 1°C cooler counterfactual path.
figure_S2_deterministic_displacement.out_of_class_interpretation: The zero-sum lag transfer is outside the fixed-allocation class. Its ratio to the delta=0.05 envelope is a descriptive scale comparison only and does not establish a bound for the out-of-class perturbation.
figure_S2_deterministic_displacement.source_data: Input tables, plotted rows and parsed-row SHA-256 hashes are recorded in qa/figure_sources_sensitivity_displacement.csv and .json.
reviewer_risks: Do not label either panel sampling coverage or interval coverage.
Do not imply that an out-of-class transfer is covered or guaranteed by the fixed-allocation envelope, even when its comparison ratio is below one.
Report the fixed allocation, candidate counts, and expected-count contrast scale.

figure_6_monthly_sensitivity.core_conclusion: At the predeclared δ=0.05, the expanded interval excludes zero only for SIM on the negative side; the other three observed monthly panels include zero.
figure_6_monthly_sensitivity.sensitivity_contract: Complete predeclared δ grid {0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.10}; fixed lag allocation weights (0.5, 0.5); finite observed factual/counterfactual basis grid only.
figure_6_monthly_sensitivity.axis: Expected count contrast: factual minus the 1°C cooler path.
figure_6_monthly_sensitivity.n_definition: Retained region-month rows are BRA 3,213; MEX 3,808; SIM 1,917; MEXD 3,808.
figure_6_monthly_sensitivity.uncertainty_definition: Vertical intervals are approximate base 90% model intervals expanded by deterministic finite-grid sensitivity radii. They are not empirical coverage intervals or Monte Carlo intervals.
reviewer_risks: Do not claim a continuous-temperature certificate.
Do not imply causal identification.
Do not call the outcome disease burden or incidence.

figure_5_daily_mvn.core_conclusion: Compare daily normal-Wald, linear-Gaussian and valid-MVN-exact procedures using only final formal analysis results.
reviewer_risks: Use actual source columns and paired-denominator definitions.
Do not imply methods were comparable when MVN V failed PSD validity.
